title: Is ChatGPT Fair for Recommendation? Evaluating Fairness in Large Language Model Recommendation

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the similarity of recommendation lists (e.g., music and movies) generated from neutral prompts versus prompts explicitly stating the user's age attribute (e.g., middle aged, old, young) using metrics like Jaccard similarity, SERP*, and PRAG*.

Comparing the similarity of recommendation lists generated from neutral prompts versus prompts explicitly stating the user's country or continent attribute (e.g., American, Chinese, African, Asian) using list similarity metrics.
Comparing the similarity of recommendation lists generated from neutral prompts versus prompts explicitly stating the user's gender (e.g., boy, girl, male, female) using list similarity metrics.

Comparing the similarity of recommendation lists generated from neutral prompts versus prompts explicitly stating the user's occupation (e.g., doctor, student, teacher, worker, writer) using list similarity metrics.

Comparing the similarity of recommendation lists generated from neutral prompts versus prompts explicitly stating the user's race (e.g., African American, black, white, yellow) using list similarity metrics.

Comparing the similarity of recommendation lists generated from neutral prompts versus prompts explicitly stating the user's religion (e.g., Buddhist, Christian, Islamic) using list similarity metrics.

Comparing the similarity of recommendation lists generated from neutral prompts versus prompts explicitly stating the user's physical attributes (referred to as 'physics' in the paper, e.g., fat, thin) using list similarity metrics.
